source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
It is crucial to specify the date and time the accessibility audit was conducted, ensuring accuracy of the assessment.
3. Provide a detailed description of the building, including its address, name, building type, and other relevant identifiers to remove any ambiguity for future reference.
4. Mention the name and contact information of the inspecting professional responsible for conducting the assessment, ensuring credibility and accountability.
5. Use a standardized accessibility checklist appropriate for your jurisdiction, assigning a checklist reference number for easy identification.
6. Record each area or item assessed along with its corresponding accessibility standard or guideline reference (e.g., ADA, ABA, etc.). This establishes the criteria used for the evaluation.
7. Document each failed check, categorizing failures by accessibility feature or aspect. Use specific, objective, and quantifiable observations.
8. For each failure, describe precisely what the issue is, noting measurements and distances where applicable, as well as inconsistencies with the standards, using clear language devoid
